name: The Molkenkur Linden

location.address: Molkenkur, Heidelberg (below the Schlosshotel Molkenkur, on the Königstuhl slope above the castle)

access: Free, public viewpoint area at Molkenkur; no ticket needed to reach or stand by the tree.
transport: Heidelberg funicular (Bergbahn) from Kornmarkt to the Molkenkur stop, a few minutes; also reachable on foot via the Klingentor path from the castle, roughly 15-20 minutes uphill.
verify_notes: Two independent sources: the Baden-Wurttemberg state Naturdenkmal register (LUBW, via the Wikipedia list that reproduces it, designated 1958-10-02, official object 82210001216) confirms existence, designation and the name 'Linde Molkenkur'; the Rhein-Neckar-Zeitung (local newspaper) ran a dedicated piece, 'Heidelberger Baumgeschichten: Die Molkenkur-Linde ist seit 20 Jahren festgezurrt', which independently describes the tree as roughly 200 years old, hollow inside but completely vital ('innen hohl, aber vollkommen vital'), and cabled/strapped together for the last 20 years to hold the crown, protected and never to be felled. Neither source gives species down to Tilia cordata vs platyphyllos, girth or exact age, so the age given here is broad and taken directly from the newspaper's own characterisation rather than derived or measured; do not sharpen it. Coordinates are LUBW's own map-tile-centre-derived figure, not a tree-level GPS fix, hence approximate. The tree stands near the upper Bergbahn (funicular) station and the Schlosshotel Molkenkur, a well-known Heidelberg viewpoint, so the general area is not in doubt even though the exact trunk position within it is not confirmed to the metre.

name: The Schlossberg Beech

location.address: Schlossberg, in the Heidelberg Schlossgarten (castle garden), below/around the castle terraces

access: Free. The Schlossgarten (castle garden and terraces) is open to the public daily in daylight hours at no charge; only the castle courtyard itself, the Grosses Fass and the Apothecary Museum need the paid Schlossticket.
transport: Short uphill walk from Kornmarkt via Kurzer Buckel, or the Bergbahn funicular from Kornmarkt to the Schloss stop.
verify_notes: Only one genuinely independent source found this pass: the Baden-Wurttemberg state Naturdenkmal register (LUBW, via the Wikipedia list, designated 1939-11-17, object 82210001201, name 'Rotbuche Schlossberg'), cross-checked directly against LUBW's own steckbrief page (matches). No age, girth or description text is carried by the register itself (its own 'kein Dokument zu diesem Objekt vorhanden'). A separate, independently published piece on beeches in Baden-Wurttemberg's state castle gardens (nussbaum.de/lokalmatador.de, 'Rotbuchen in den Schlossgaerten von Baden-Wuerttemberg') describes 14 mature Rotbuchen standing at the Scheffelterrasse on the edge of the Heidelberg Schlossgarten, i.e. the same immediate area as this register coordinate, and says the garden holds century-old trees generally. That corroborates that old red beeches genuinely stand in this part of the garden, but it names an ensemble of 14 rather than this one designated specimen, so it is context rather than a second confirming source for THIS tree specifically. Flagged for that reason. 'Rotbuche' is simply the German common name for the European beech (Fagus sylvatica), not necessarily a copper-leaved cultivar; recorded here under the canonical species name.

name: The Neuenheimer Landstrasse Swamp Cypress

location.address: Neuenheimer Landstrasse, Neuenheim, along the north bank of the Neckar

access: Free. A street tree on Neuenheimer Landstrasse, a public riverside road with a pavement/cycle path; viewable at any time.
transport: Short walk along the Neckar's north bank from the Alte Bruecke (Old Bridge), Neuenheim side; also served by Neuenheim bus and tram stops.
verify_notes: Single genuinely independent source this pass: the Baden-Wurttemberg state Naturdenkmal register (LUBW, via the Wikipedia list, designated 1942-07-28, object 82210001206, name 'Sumpfzypresse Neuenheimer Landstrasse'), cross-checked against LUBW's own steckbrief page (matches exactly). No age, girth or description carried by the register. Note the honest distinction: Heidelberg's own green-space authority (stadtgruen-hd.de, 'Exotische Baeume') separately documents swamp cypresses at the Tertiaergaertchen in Neuenheimer Feld, by the Institute for Earth Sciences (INF 235), a DIFFERENT site several hundred metres from Neuenheimer Landstrasse; that page does not describe this specific register tree, and the two are not conflated here. Species recorded as Taxodium distichum, the common bald/swamp cypress and the species this German common name (Sumpfzypresse) usually denotes in local registers, though the register does not specify the binomial itself; flagged accordingly, and the page should invite a reader to confirm on the ground if it matters (T. distichum vs T. ascendens).

name: The Zwingerstrasse Horse Chestnuts

location.address: Zwingerstrasse, Altstadt, between Kettengasse and Burgweg, near the funicular's Talstation

access: Free. Zwingerstrasse is an ordinary public street in the Altstadt, a few minutes' walk from Kornmarkt and the Bergbahn funicular's lower station.
transport: A few minutes' walk from Kornmarkt or the Bergbahn Talstation.
verify_notes: Single genuinely independent source this pass: the state Naturdenkmal register (LUBW, via the Wikipedia list, designated 1986-02-03, object 82210001225, register name 'Rosskastanien Zwingerstrasse' on Wikipedia / 'Rosskastanien Zwingerstrasse' on the LUBW steckbrief, matching). This is registered as a small stand of horse chestnuts at one point rather than a single trunk; treat it as one compact, collectible ensemble at one obvious place to stand, per the project's ensemble rule, not as an avenue. No age, girth or description carried by either register document. Confirmed Zwingerstrasse is a normal public Altstadt street (not private grounds) via general street directories.

name: The Bergstrasse Crimean Linden
access: Free. Bergstrasse is an ordinary public residential street in Neuenheim; the tree stands as a street tree, viewable from the pavement.
transport: A short walk from Neuenheim's Bergstrasse/Blumenthalstrasse bus stops.
verify_notes: Single genuinely independent source this pass: the state Naturdenkmal register (LUBW, via the Wikipedia list, designated 1986-08-04, object 82210001227, name 'Krimlinde Bergstrasse'), cross-checked against LUBW's own steckbrief page (matches). No age, girth or description of THIS specimen carried by the register. General species facts (Tilia x euchlora, a Tilia cordata x dasystyla hybrid dating to around 1860, typically 15-18m tall) come from horticultural nursery sources describing the cultivar in general, not this tree specifically, and are included in case useful for the story but are not tree-specific verification. A second Naturdenkmal, '2 Zypressen (Nutka- und Scheinzypresse) Bergstrasse', sits at essentially the same coordinate (49.4183,8.6922) and was not researched this pass; noted as a lead for a possible companion entry.

name: The Ringstrasse Oak

location.address: Ringstrasse, near the Ringstrasse tram stop, Kirchheim/Bahnstadt

access: Free. Ringstrasse is a public street served by tram line 26 (Ringstrasse stop); the tree is a street tree, viewable at any time.
transport: Tram line 26 to the Ringstrasse stop, then on foot.
verify_notes: Single genuinely independent source this pass: the state Naturdenkmal register (LUBW, via the Wikipedia list, designated 1958-10-14, object 82210001217, name 'Eiche Ringstrasse'), cross-checked against LUBW's own steckbrief page (matches). Species recorded only as 'Oak (Quercus sp.)' deliberately: the register names it plainly 'Eiche' (oak), NOT 'Stieleiche' (pedunculate oak) as it does for three other Heidelberg oaks on the same list (Stieleiche am Aukopf, Stieleiche Muenchelstrasse (1) and (2), Stieleiche Orthopaedie), which is a real naming distinction in the same source rather than an inconsistency to smooth over. Do not silently assume Quercus robur. The page should ask the reader which oak this is. No age or girth data found. Confirmed Ringstrasse is a public street/tram stop, not private grounds, via general directory sources; this candidate sits furthest from the Altstadt cluster of the six delivered here (roughly 2 to 2.5km from the Marktplatz), so if the city page groups by walkable cluster, this one may belong to a second, separate stop rather than the main Altstadt/Schlossberg/Neuenheim walk.
